title: Snapshot-based rolling upgrade with soft-quiesce and tenant backfill windows
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement an upgrade orchestrator that performs rolling upgrades of GPU pools using lightweight snapshots and a soft-quiesce phase. The goal is to preserve capacity for latency-sensitive tenants, allow bounded backfill for best-effort workloads, and coordinate with the autoscaler to avoid surge or underprovisioning during upgrades. This ticket covers design, implementation hooks in the upgrade controller, integration with the autoscaler handshake, and the first staged rollout on canary pools.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator can create a lightweight 'node snapshot' capturing KV cache eviction points and live-connection drain markers before reboots.
Soft-quiesce window implemented: new admission is throttled per-tenant while existing in-flight sessions finish within configurable duration.
Backfill window policy allows low-priority workloads to utilize freed slots but enforces an eviction budget so high-priority tenants remain below SLA thresholds.

Autoscaler handshake implemented: orchestrator signals planned drain windows and autoscaler responds with temporary cushion or admission limits; no more than 5% SLA regression in 95th percentile latency in canary.
Runbook and automated rollback exist; rollout run on two canary pools without customer-visible degradation.
Metrics dashboards show admission throttle, backfill utilization, eviction rate, and autoscaler cushion events.
End-to-end e2e test in CI simulates 3 concurrent pool upgrades with mixed tenant load and validates no token-loss and bounded latency impact.
technical_design: High-level design: (1) Snapshot phase: before cordon, the node agent produces a small upgrade snapshot capturing KV-cache prefix hashes, latest model-weights checksum, and soft-quiesce cursor for active sessions. (2) Soft-quiesce phase: controller applies a per-tenant admission controller that gradually reduces new session admits to a target rate over a configurable backoff (default 30s), allowing existing sessions to flush. (3) Backfill windows: freed slots are advertised as 'best-effort' to the admission controller; a priority queue assigns these to low-priority tenants with an eviction budget counter. (4) Autoscaler handshake: orchestrator announces planned capacity delta (expected unavailable GPUs) via a new API to the autoscaler; autoscaler either temporarily increases pool target or returns a negative acknowledgement leading orchestrator to delay. (5) Roll step: perform upgrade, validate health probes, restore node state from snapshot and uncordon. Trade-offs: snapshotting avoids full KV dump cost but requires careful compatibility checks; soft-quiesce increases service latency tail if misconfigured, so defaults are conservative. Implementation touches: upgrade-controller, node-agent, admission-controller, autoscaler-adapter, and console metrics exporter.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal testing in staging - run 5 repeated upgrades against synthetic workloads (2/3 latency-sensitive, 1/3 batch) (3 days).
Phase 1: Canary pools - select 2 small dedicated pools with low critical tenants, enable orchestrator with backfill enabled (1 week).
Phase 2: Incremental rollout - 10% of pools per day, monitor dashboard and rollback on >3% sustained 95th percentile latency or >1% error increase (2 weeks).
Phase 3: Full fleet with staggered windows and cross-region coordination; final validation and docs (3 days).
testing_plan: Unit tests for snapshot serialization and admission throttle logic.
Integration test: simulate autoscaler negative ack and ensure orchestrator delays upgrade.
Load test: 48-hour run in canary with focused 95th/99th latency tracking and pre/post comparisons.
Chaos test: randomly preempt nodes during soft-quiesce to validate eviction budget enforcement and backfill recovery.
